summary: The site for Maple Mono, an open-source rounded monospace font with a cursive italic, by a single developer (subframe7536): a narrow, dark slate single column with a gradient wordmark, a first-person 'Why another one?', feature cards whose switches toggle the actual OpenType features (cv01, cv04, zero, cursive italic, ligatures, [TODO]-style tag ligatures), a tabbed comparison against JetBrains Mono, Fira Code and Iosevka, a grid of real code snippets, a testimonial carousel and generous credits. Downloading and the full playground live on sub-pages.

instances.look: Fixed translucent bar with backdrop blur: maple-leaf icon, WHY · FEATURES · PREVIEW · CREDITS anchors with animated underlines at left; GitHub, Playground, Usage (icon + label) and a light-blue 'Get Font' button at right (repeated across the stitched crops)
instances.ux: Anchors scroll inside the main scroller; Get Font goes to /en/download, Playground to the full tester
instances.learn: Keep the heavy tools (playground, usage docs, downloads) on their own pages and link them from a small fixed bar, so the landing page stays a story

reconstruction.layout: Fixed full-width bar ~48px, bg-background/50 + backdrop-blur-lg; links as 32px-high ghost buttons with 16px padding
reconstruction.typography: ~12–14px Maple Mono, weight 500, caps for anchors
reconstruction.html: nav.fixed.backdrop-blur-lg > a > img + div (a[href=#why] … ) + div (a GitHub, a Playground, a Usage, a Get Font)

instances.look: 'Why Another One?' in mint, a paragraph and a bullet list naming what the author dislikes in other coding fonts (JetBrains Mono too rigid, Fira Code's synthetic italic angle, Victor Mono's exaggerated cursive, Sarasa Gothic too narrow, few rounded corners, little Nerd-Font/CJK support), then 'Therefore, I created this font with clean glyphs, a cursive-style italic, fine-grained configuration, built-in Nerd-Font, and a 2:1 ratio for Chinese and English'
instances.learn: Frame the brief as a list of honest complaints about named rivals: every complaint becomes a design requirement the page can then prove

instances.look: Two feature groups as a 2-column grid of cards: 'Distinct Glyphs, Smooth Design' (@ $ & % → with a 'cv01' switch; cursive f i l k x y with a 'plain style' switch; I 1 l with 'cv04'; O 0 o with 'zero'), and 'Smart Ligatures, Large Variety' (a 'Ligature ON | Ligature OFF' segmented tab above three rows of mint ligatures interleaved with dim letters: <>a??b≢c…d↦), then 'Special Ligatures' cards: pill-shaped DEBUG INFO WARN ERROR TODO FIXME tags (calt), connected italic 'all class / ultra suffix' (calt), smart spacing '1>>4 / Vec<R<T>>' (calt); each card has a one-line grey note
instances.ux: Every switch toggles that card's real OpenType feature(s) (e.g. 'plain style' flips cv32–cv37 on the italic; [DEBUG] turns into a pill only with calt on); the ligature tabs toggle calt on the three rows
instances.learn: Put a labelled switch with the feature tag under each sample: visitors learn the tag names they'll need in their editor config while playing
